title: What if a long division never reaches a remainder of zero?
description: Two decimal divisions are each turned into a division by a counting number by multiplying both numbers by ten or a hundred. A long division then shows that the remainder keeps coming back, so the digits of the answer never end. Multiplying back checks the first answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a remainder comes back, the digits of the answer never end, and we stop after a few places. Watch for students who keep dividing in the hope that a zero remainder will come.

video_script.why: The child can divide by a counting number but expects every long division to stop at a remainder of zero.
video_script.substitution: Both numbers are multiplied by ten or a hundred, and when a remainder comes back, the digits never end.
video_script.anchor: Twenty four point eight six divided by one point two, and five point seven two eight divided by one point five two
video_script.payoff_line: The second quotient is three point seven six eight four two one, and the digits never end.

final_answer.spoken: twenty point seven one six six six and so on, and three point seven six eight four two one and so on

video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 248.6/12 is read two hundred and forty eight point six over twelve, and 572.8/152 is five hundred and seventy two point eight over a hundred and fifty two.
maths_rules: 248 Ones / 12 = 20 Ones rem 8; 86 Tenths / 12 = 7 Tenths rem 2; 20 Hundredths / 12 = 1 rem 8; 80 Thousandths / 12 = 6 rem 8; the remainder 8 comes back, so 20.71666...
video_script.design: The two divisions stay on the board; both numbers are multiplied by ten or a hundred, and the long division is run until the digits are seen to go on.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; two divisions 24.86 ÷ 1.2 and 5.728 ÷ 1.52, each with an empty answer box
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing decimals.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first is twenty four point eight six divided by one point two.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second is five point seven two eight divided by one point five two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are these two quotients?

beats.on_screen: the two divisions and their empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Both numbers are multiplied by 10 or 100 until the number we divide by is a counting number; a remainder that comes back is circled

marks.same: both numbers move together to make the number we divide by a counting number
marks.back: a remainder that comes back is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. Multiply both numbers by ten or a hundred, and then use long division.
<bookmark mark='back'/>If the same remainder comes back, the digits of the answer never end.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two divisions. Twenty four point eight six divided by one point two. <bookmark mark='given2'/>Five point seven two eight divided by one point five two.

marks.find: the two answer boxes are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find both quotients.

marks.s1b: both numbers are multiplied by 10 and 248.6 over 12 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, the first division, twenty four point eight six divided by one point two.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Multiply both numbers by ten. We get two hundred and forty eight point six over twelve.

beats.on_screen: 248.6 ÷ 12: 248 Ones ÷ 12 = 20 Ones, 8 Ones remain; 8 Ones + 6 Tenths = 86 Tenths; 86 Tenths ÷ 12 = 7 Tenths, 2 Tenths remain

marks.s2a: 248.6 ÷ 12 is set in a long division frame
marks.s2b: twenty Ones go to the answer and eight Ones remain
marks.s2c: eight Ones and six Tenths make eighty six Tenths, and seven Tenths go to the answer

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, a long division of two hundred and forty eight point six by twelve.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Two hundred and forty eight Ones divided by twelve gives twenty Ones, and eight Ones remain.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Eight Ones and six Tenths make eighty six Tenths. Eighty six Tenths divided by twelve gives seven Tenths, and two Tenths remain.

beats.on_screen: 2 Tenths = 20 Hundredths; 20 ÷ 12 = 1, 8 remain; 8 Hundredths = 80 Thousandths; 80 ÷ 12 = 6, 8 remain again; the remainder 8 is circled; 24.86 ÷ 1.2 = 20.71666...

marks.s3a: the two Tenths regroup into twenty Hundredths and one goes to the answer
marks.s3b: the eight that remain regroup into eighty Thousandths and six go to the answer
marks.s3c: the remainder eight is circled each time it comes back
marks.s3d: three dots follow the first answer

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, regroup the two Tenths into twenty Hundredths. Twenty Hundredths divided by twelve gives one Hundredth, and eight remain.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Regroup them into eighty Thousandths. Eighty Thousandths divided by twelve gives six Thousandths, and eight remain again.

<bookmark mark='s3c'/>The remainder eight keeps coming back, and the digit six keeps coming too. <bookmark mark='s3d'/>The first answer is twenty point seven one six six six, and its digits never end.

marks.s4b: both numbers are multiplied by 100 and 572.8 over 152 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, the second division, five point seven two eight divided by one point five two.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Multiply both numbers by a hundred. We get five hundred and seventy two point eight over a hundred and fifty two.

beats.on_screen: 572.8 ÷ 152: 572 Ones ÷ 152 = 3 Ones, 116 Ones remain; then 7 Tenths, 6 Hundredths, 8 Thousandths, 4, 2, 1, ...; the remainders do not reach 0

marks.s5a: 572.8 ÷ 152 is set in a long division frame and three Ones go to the answer
marks.s5b: the next digits are written one by one in their places
marks.s5c: three dots follow the digits because no remainder is zero

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, a long division by a hundred and fifty two. Five hundred and seventy two Ones gives three Ones, and a hundred and sixteen Ones remain.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>The next digits are seven Tenths, six Hundredths, eight Thousandths, and then four, two and one.
<bookmark mark='s5c'/>Each step leaves a remainder, and the digits never end.
<bookmark mark='s6a'/>Step six, check the first answer by multiplying back.
<bookmark mark='s6b'/>Twelve times twenty point seven one six six is almost two hundred and forty eight point six. That matches the number we began with.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The second quotient is three point seven six eight four two one, and the digits never end.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The first quotient is twenty point seven one six six six, and its digits never end too.
